newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings to make Robinson momentoes - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings to make Robinson momentoes - CFO.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Inc has struck a deal to make Jackie Robinson commerative baseballs to mark the black player's major league debut 50 years ago, chief financial officer Paul Martin said on Friday.
"Some of the proceeds will go to the Jackie Robinson Foundation," Martin said in a telephone interview.
Each of the 28 major league teams will use the Robinson balls during their opening-day home games during April, Martin said.
Robinson was the first black to play in the majors, a watershed in U.S. race relations.
A formal announcement of the deal, similar to one made last year with the estate of late Yankee great Mickey Mantle, will be made next week, Martin said.
Martin declined to discuss financial details, other than to say the Robinson ball would likely retail for around $30.

The company is also negotiating to issue commerative balls marking the 56th anniversary this year of Yankee legend Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak. Now in his 80s, DiMaggio hit at least once in 56 straight games.
"The talks are ongoing but the ultimate outcome is still unknown," Martin said of the DiMaggio bargaining.
